final_message:
**Status: partial.** The function is recovered and holds on held-out inputs, but the circuit is not verified: I could not show any head or MLP layer to be inert. Everything below was measured on `local-full` (full precision).

**Algorithm**

The model outputs the highest-priority symbol present among the four inputs, with a fixed order:

```python
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    order = [6, 4, 5, 2, 7, 3]   # pi > po > pu > pa > re > li
    present = set(tokens[1:])
    for t in order:
        if t in present:
            return t
```

**Verification numbers**

| Check | V0001: all 6 components | V0002: head 1.0 dropped |
|---|---|---|
| Agreement of `predict()` with the model (400 held-out) | 400/400 (null ≈ 0.35) | 400/400 |
| Circuit ablated: logit diff left / accuracy | 1.7% / 0.485 | 2.4% / 0.4875 |
| Everything else ablated: logit diff left / accuracy | 100% / 1.0 (trivial, nothing left to ablate) | 64.6% / 0.9925 |
| Lab status | not-verified: no sufficiency null can be drawn for a whole-model circuit | not-verified: 64.6% is below the 70% threshold |

**What the experiments show about the mechanism**

- **No inert component at this granularity.** Mean-ablating any single head leaves 55–67% of the logit difference; mlp0 alone leaves 19% and mlp1 33%. This contradicts the task's premise at head/MLP level; any dead weight would have to be at neuron or subspace level, which I did not examine.
- **Layer 0 only produces a weak tentative answer.** After layer 0 the logit difference is 2.0 of the final 38.7, and the layer-0 heads have almost no direct effect on the logits (about 0.005 each).
- **Layer 1 writes mainly through mlp1.** Heads 1.0 and 1.1 have direct effects of 0.10–0.11 against total effects of 0.36–0.50.
- **Attention is selective only for high-priority symbols.** With pi present, both layer-1 heads put 0.78 of their attention on it. With pa as the winner among li/re, attention is diffuse (0.39 and 0.33, not on the winner), so low-priority cases are resolved some other way, presumably in the MLPs; I did not explain how.
- **Margin versus accuracy.** Head 1.0 is needed for the margin but barely for the answer: accuracy stays at 0.9925 without it.

**Prediction record**

Of 10 pre-registrations, 9 ran: 7 confirmed, 2 refuted (hit rate 0.78). The tenth errored because `path_patching` did not accept an MLP as sender; I replaced it with a heads-only version.

- **Refuted, li vs re:** I guessed li outranks re; the model prefers re on all 14 mixed li/re inputs, by a small margin of 2–9 logits.
- **Refuted, attention rule:** I predicted layer-1 heads would attend to the winner even when it is pa; they do not.

**Budget:** 15 of 25 experiments used, plus the 2 verifications.

**Report:** `benchmarks\glassbox-bench\seed-2\runs\t7\report\report.md` (with `report.html` alongside).
